role: Household storm claims intake handler at a home insurer, reviewing each newly lodged claim file before it is routed
setting: A regional home insurer receives storm damage claims after wind, hail and heavy rain events. The intake handler opens one claim file at a time. The file holds policy details, the claimant's loss report, an automated weather lookup, property history, a contractor estimate and a checklist of lodged documents. The handler checks whether the storm is corroborated and whether damage predates it. They then decide how the claim proceeds and how urgently make-safe work is needed. Signals are often indirect: dates in one section must be compared with dates in another, estimates with benchmarks, and survey notes with the claimed damage area.

weather_corroborated.instructions: Recorded weather at the property supports a storm on the loss date.

criteria.true: Station data near property shows qualifying storm that day.
criteria.false: No qualifying event, distant station only, or dates differ.

pre_existing_damage.instructions: File evidence shows claimed damage existed before the reported storm.

criteria.true: Earlier survey or claim records the same damage area.
criteria.false: No dated evidence places the damage before the storm.

intake_route.instructions: How should this claim proceed after intake review?

criteria.fast_track: File complete, cover and weather confirmed, estimate within benchmark.
criteria.hold_for_info: Exactly one required document or confirmation is still outstanding.
criteria.field_inspection: File complete but damage extent or cost needs on-site assessment.
criteria.refer_investigation: Dates, statements or history conflict in ways suggesting misrepresentation.

source_support.instructions: How many independent sources confirm the information in this record?
criteria: No independent source confirms the information
Exactly one independent source confirms it
Two or three independent sources confirm it
Four or more independent sources confirm it

makesafe_urgency.instructions: How urgently does the property need emergency make-safe work?
criteria: No breach to roof, walls or windows recorded
Breach recorded, temporary repair already completed
Breach open, no temporary repair, home still habitable
Breach open and home recorded as unsafe to occupy

factors.name: weather_match
factors.description: How the automated weather lookup relates to the claimed loss date and location: qualifying gusts at a nearby station on the date, a qualifying event only at a distant station, no qualifying event, or a qualifying event one or more days away from the claimed date.

factors.name: report_lag_days
factors.description: Days between the claimed loss date and the date the claim was lodged; long lags are alarming but can be explained by the claimant being away.

factors.name: policy_status
factors.description: Policy state at the loss date: active with storm cover, within a lapse grace period, storm cover excluded by endorsement, or policy inception dated after the loss date (out-of-order dates).

factors.name: prior_condition_evidence
factors.description: What property history shows about the claimed damage area before the storm: nothing on file, a clean dated survey, a survey noting wear in the same area, or a previous claim on the same area that was never repaired.

factors.name: missing_item
factors.description: Which required intake item is absent: none, damage photos, contractor estimate (estimate section null), proof of ownership, or two items at once.

factors.name: estimate_ratio
factors.description: Contractor estimate total divided by the insurer's desk benchmark for the declared damage; high values are alarming.

factors.name: estimate_uplift_explained
factors.description: Whether the file carries a benign reason for a high estimate, such as listed-building materials, scaffold access or post-storm labour surcharge noted by the contractor and matched by a property flag.

factors.name: envelope_breach_state
factors.description: State of the building envelope after the storm: no breach, breach with temporary repair done, breach open but occupied, breach open and recorded unsafe.

factors.name: temp_repair_dated_before_loss
factors.description: Whether a temporary repair invoice is dated before the claimed loss date, an out-of-order sign that the damage predates the storm or the date is wrong.

factors.name: prior_claims_3y
factors.description: Number of storm or water claims on this property in the last three years.

factors.name: prior_claims_verified
factors.description: Whether earlier claims were each settled against a verified named storm, which lowers concern about repeat claiming.

factors.name: statement_consistency
factors.description: How the claimant's free-text statement fits the rest of the file: consistent, minor discrepancy (time of day, which room), or contradicting photos or weather timing.

factors.name: claimant_away_note
factors.description: Whether the statement explains a long reporting lag (holiday, hospital stay, second home), mitigating report_lag_days.

sections.name: policy
sections.description: Policy number, inception and renewal dates, status, storm cover flag, excess, endorsements.

sections.name: loss_report
sections.description: Loss date, lodged date, peril, damaged areas list, occupancy state, and the claimant's short free-text statement.

sections.name: weather_check
sections.description: Automated lookup: station id, distance_km, event_date, max_gust_mph, rain_mm, hail_flag, threshold_met.

sections.name: property_history
sections.description: Property flags, last survey date and short survey note, and a list of prior claims with dates, areas and settlement basis.

sections.name: estimate
sections.description: Contractor estimate total, desk benchmark, line items, temp repair entries with dates, short contractor note; null when not supplied.

sections.name: intake_docs
sections.description: Checklist of required documents with received booleans and received dates.

rendering_notes: weather_match: weather_check.event_date and distance_km compared with loss_report.loss_date; confirmed_near = same date, distance_km under 10, threshold_met true; distant_station_only = threshold_met true but distance_km 25-60; date_offset = event_date 1-4 days from loss_date; no_event = threshold_met false with low max_gust_mph. Never write 'corroborated' anywhere. report_lag_days: shown only as loss_report.loss_date versus lodged_date. claimant_away_note appears as a sentence in loss_report.claimant_statement (e.g. 'We were abroad until the 14th and found the ceiling down on return'); absent otherwise. policy_status: policy.status plus policy.inception_date; incepted_after_loss shows an inception date later than loss_date with status 'active' (decoy: status looks fine); storm_excluded shows endorsements list containing 'END-STX storm exclusion' while storm_cover may be omitted. prior_condition_evidence: property_history.last_survey_date (before loss) and survey_note (e.g. 'rear slope tiles slipped, ridge mortar failing'); damaged areas in loss_report must be compared with note and prior_claims[].area; unrepaired_prior_claim shows a prior claim on the same area with settlement 'cash_settled' and no repair_completed date. missing_item: intake_docs entries with received false; contractor_estimate missing renders the estimate section as null; two_items marks two entries false. estimate_ratio: estimate.total versus estimate.desk_benchmark, never as a ratio field. estimate_uplift_explained: estimate.contractor_note mentions listed slate or scaffold access AND property_history.flags includes 'listed_building' or 'three_storey'; when false the note is generic or empty. envelope_breach_state: loss_report.occupancy ('occupied','occupied_partial','vacated_unsafe') plus damaged_areas items with breach booleans and estimate.temp_repairs entries; temp_repaired shows a dated tarpaulin or boarding line. temp_repair_dated_before_loss: a temp_repairs date earlier than loss_date. prior_claims_3y: length of property_history.prior_claims within three years; prior_claims_verified appears as each claim's settlement_basis 'named_storm_verified' versus 'claimant_account'. statement_consistency: the claimant_statement mentions a time, room or cause that matches or conflicts with damaged_areas, weather timing or photo captions in intake_docs. Decoys: vulnerable-occupant flag in loss_report, policy excess size, hail_flag when only wind damage is claimed, rain_mm alone, high prior_claims_3y when verified, long lag when explained. No field may state a route, urgency, fraud suspicion or pre-existence verdict; free text uses plain first-person or trade wording, at most one sentence each, three free-text fields maximum.
